title: Coil: portal Snake with seeded apples, border gaps, gold apples, step mode, replays and a top-5 table
prompt:
Build a modern Snake game called Coil on a canvas: a dark slate board with a faint checker, a lime snake with a darker outline whose head has eyes facing the direction of travel, red apples, a shining gold apple, grey rocks, and two pairs of glowing portal rings (A cyan, B magenta). Keep drawing light (no per-pixel effects, at most a few particles) so it runs smoothly on a laptop without a GPU.

The arena is 24 columns x 18 rows (row 1 on top, column 1 on the left) and is exactly this map ('#' rock, '.' floor, 'A' and 'B' portals):
###########..###########
#......................#
#..A................B..#
#......................#
#.....####....####.....#
#......................#
#......................#
#..........##..........#
...........##...........
#..........##..........#
#......................#
#......................#
#.....####....####.....#
#......................#
#......................#
#..B................A..#
#......................#
###########..###########

Snake: it starts with its head at row 9, column 6 and its body at columns 5 and 4, facing right, and waits for the first direction key (arrow keys or WASD). It moves one cell per step. A key that would reverse it onto its neck is ignored, and up to two turns pressed between steps are queued. Stepping onto a portal puts the head on the other portal of the same color, keeping its direction; the body follows through. Leaving the map through a gap in the border re-enters on the opposite side. Hitting a rock or its own body ends the game, but moving into the cell the tail is leaving on that same step is allowed.

Apples: randomness comes from mulberry32(seed), with a Seed field (default 1) and ?seed=N in the URL.
function mulberry32(a){return function(){a|=0;a=a+0x6D2B79F5|0;let t=Math.imul(a^a>>>15,1|a);t=t+Math.imul(t^t>>>7,61|t)^t;return((t^t>>>14)>>>0)/4294967296;}}
To place an item, list the free floor cells (not rock, portal, snake or another item) in reading order (row 1 left to right, then row 2 …) and take index floor(rand() x count). One red apple is always on the board: the first is placed when a game is set up, and each next one right after the step that ate the previous one (so the new head, and the tail, which stays put when eating, count as snake). Red apple number k scores 10 x (1 + floor((k - 1) / 5)): 10 each for apples 1-5, 20 for 6-10 and so on. Right after the replacement for every 5th red apple is placed, a gold apple is placed too: it scores 50, adds 3 segments (the tail stays put for 3 steps) and vanishes after 40 steps, blinking during its last 10.

Speed: min(14, 6 + 0.5 x red apples eaten) steps per second, shown in the HUD as 'Speed 6.0'.

Step mode (a checkbox, the T key or ?step=1) is for practice: the snake moves exactly one step per direction key press and never on its own; everything else, including the gold apple's 40 steps, works the same.

HUD: Score, Length, Apples (red apples eaten), Speed and Best. P pauses ('PAUSED') and R restarts with the same seed. Game over shows 'GAME OVER' with the cause ('Hit a rock' or 'Hit yourself'), the score and length, and a 'Watch replay' button that replays the whole game from its first step at 10 steps per second from the recorded key presses, ending on the same final state. Keep a TOP 5 (name, score, length, seed) in localStorage; a finished game that makes the table asks for a name. Step-mode games are practice: show 'PRACTICE' in the HUD and never record them.
interaction_hints: Each interact call opens a fresh page. Use --entry 'index.html?seed=253&step=1' (step mode: exactly one step per key press; use press actions with delay_ms 80). Rows/columns are 1-based as in the map. All facts below were computed with the stated rules. Seed 253: the first apple is at row 7 col 9 on every fresh page. Notation U2 = ArrowUp twice, R3 = ArrowRight three times, etc. From the start U2 R3 eats it: Score 10, Length 4, Apples 1, next apple at row 9 col 18. Tail rule: continue with D1 L1 U1 R1 D1 L1 U1 R1 (the 4-segment snake circles a 2x2 square, the head entering the cell the tail leaves): still alive, Score 10. Self hit (fresh page): U2 R3 R9 D2 (2nd apple; next at row 9 col 23) then L1 U1 R1 -> 'Hit yourself', Score 20. Full line (fresh page): U2 R3 | R9 D2 | R5 (apple 3, next at row 9 col 1) | R2 (the head leaves through the row 9 gap on the right and re-enters at col 1: apple 4, next at row 9 col 3) | R2 (apple 5: next red at row 3 col 23 and a gold apple at row 4 col 9) | U5 R6 (gold, +50) | R13 U1 R1 (apple 6, worth 20): Score 120, Length 12, Apples 6, 'Speed 9.0'. Gold expiry (fresh page): U2 R3 R9 D2 R5 R2 R2 then D2 R8 D1 L8 D2 R10 D2 L7 (40 steps after the gold appears): it blinks during the last 10 and is gone after the 40th. Rock: fresh page, press ArrowRight 6 times -> 'Hit a rock' on the 6th press (head at col 11). Reverse: fresh page, ArrowLeft does nothing. Portal: fresh page, U6 L2 -> the head enters portal A at row 3 col 4 and appears on its partner at row 16 col 21 while the body is still at row 3 cols 5-6; one more ArrowLeft -> head at row 16 col 20. Replay: after a game over click 'Watch replay', screenshot at ~1 s and at the end: same final state. Real time: plain ?seed=253, press ArrowDown, screenshots at ~0.5 s and ~1 s: about 3 and 6 cells travelled, 'Speed 6.0'; quick turns: press ArrowUp, wait 40, press ArrowRight within one step: both turns are taken. TOP 5: plain ?seed=253, press ArrowUp, wait ~250 ms (adjust 200-400 so the snake climbs exactly two rows), press ArrowRight: it eats the apple (10) and runs into the rock at row 7 col 24 -> GAME OVER, type a name, submit, reload action, check the TOP 5; a step-mode game shows 'PRACTICE' and is never recorded. Pause: p, two screenshots 500 ms apart unchanged.

rubric.criterion: The arena matches the given 24x18 map: border gaps at row 9 and columns 12-13, the four rock bars and the centre block, cyan A portals at row 3 col 4 and row 16 col 21, magenta B portals at row 3 col 21 and row 16 col 4, and the snake starting on row 9 columns 4-6 facing right.
With ?seed=253 the first apple is at row 7 col 9 on every fresh page, and in step mode U2 R3 eats it (Score 10, Length 4) with the next apple at row 9 col 18.

The full seed 253 hint line reproduces exactly: apples at row 9 cols 23, 1 and 3 across the row 9 border gap, a gold apple at row 4 col 9 with the 5th apple, and after the 6th apple Score 120, Length 12, Apples 6 and 'Speed 9.0'.
Portals work: in step mode U6 L2 puts the head on row 16 col 21 with the body still near row 3, and one more ArrowLeft moves it to row 16 col 20.
The tail rule holds: after the first apple the 4-segment snake circles a 2x2 square for eight steps without dying, while after the second apple L1 U1 R1 ends with 'Hit yourself'.
ArrowRight six times from the start ends with 'Hit a rock' on the 6th press, and a reversing key (ArrowLeft at the start) is ignored.
The gold apple scores 50 and adds 3 segments, and when left alone it blinks during its last 10 steps and disappears after 40 steps.
In real time the snake moves about 6 cells per second at the start with 'Speed 6.0', two quick turns are both taken, and P pauses with 'PAUSED'.
Game over shows 'GAME OVER' with the cause, score and length, and 'Watch replay' replays the game at about 10 steps per second to the same final state.
A real-time game that scores asks for a name and appears in the TOP 5 with score, length and seed after a reload, while step-mode games show 'PRACTICE' and are never recorded.

A clean, cohesive look a game artist would accept: square cells on a subtle checker, an outlined snake with eyes facing its direction, distinct red and shining gold apples, glowing cyan and magenta portals, and a HUD that never overlaps the 1280x800 arena.

title: Drop Four: Connect Four with an exact minimax computer, position codes, threat markers and records
prompt:
Build a Connect Four game called Drop Four: a glossy blue 7 x 6 board with round holes, red and yellow discs that fall into place with a short bounce, Inter or Roboto type, and a side panel. Columns are numbered 1-7 from the left and rows 1-6 from the bottom.

Play: Red always moves first. Drop a disc by clicking a column, pressing 1-7, or moving a hover marker with Left/Right and pressing Enter, Space or Down. A full column refuses the drop with a small shake. Four or more in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally wins: ring the winning discs, dim the rest and show 'Red wins!' or 'Yellow wins!'; a full board without a win is 'Draw'. After the end no more discs can be dropped. The panel shows whose turn it is and the move number.

Position code: the panel always shows the game so far as column digits in move order (e.g. 4453). Pasting a code and pressing 'Load' replays it on an empty board; a code with a character other than 1-7, a drop into a full column, or moves after a win shows 'Invalid code' and keeps the current game.

Computer: choose 'Two players' or 'vs Computer' (you play Red or Yellow) and Easy, Medium or Hard. The computer runs minimax with alpha-beta pruning to a fixed depth: Easy 2, Medium 4, Hard 6 plies, its own move being ply 1. It tries columns in the order 4, 3, 5, 2, 6, 1, 7 and keeps the first best move. A win at ply n scores 100000 - n for the computer, a loss at ply n scores -(100000 - n), and a full board scores 0. At the depth limit a position is scored from the computer's side: for each of the 69 windows of four cells in a line, +5 if it holds 3 of its discs and 1 empty cell, +2 for 2 of its discs and 2 empty, and -4 for 3 opponent discs and 1 empty; plus 3 for each of its discs in column 4. It moves about 400 ms after you (at once when a loaded code leaves it to move), shows 'Thinking…' meanwhile, and answers within 2 seconds even on Hard.

More: 'Hint' rings the column the Hard computer would choose for the side to move. 'Show threats' draws a small ring of the matching color in every empty cell where Red or Yellow would complete four, even if that cell cannot be played yet. Undo takes back one move (vs the computer, your move and its reply). A session scoreboard counts Red wins, Yellow wins and draws, and your wins, draws and losses against each computer level are kept in localStorage.
interaction_hints: Each interact call opens a fresh page; set mode, color and level first, then type a code into the code field and click Load. All facts were computed with the stated search (alpha-beta and plain minimax agree). Wins (Two players): 1212121 -> 'Red wins!' with column 1 rows 1-4 ringed; 12233434544 -> 'Red wins!' on the diagonal col1 row1, col2 row2, col3 row3, col4 row4; 1223344345 -> 'Yellow wins!' on the bottom row columns 2-5; 562515647266514373662152213723734735174441 (42 moves) -> 'Draw'. After a win, clicking a column does nothing. Invalid: 48, 1111111 (seventh disc in column 1) and 12121212 (a move after Red's win) each show 'Invalid code' and leave the board unchanged. Block: vs Computer, you Red, load 11223 -> the computer (Yellow) plays column 4 on Easy, Medium and Hard. Opening: vs Computer, you Yellow, New game -> every level opens in column 4. Level test: vs Computer, you Red, load 241431516 (Yellow to move) on a fresh page per level: Easy plays 4, Medium plays 5, Hard plays 3 (Hard's root values: column 3 and column 1 are forced wins at ply 5; column 3 comes first in the order). After Hard's 3, whatever column Red plays, Hard Yellow wins within its next two moves (e.g. Red 1 -> Yellow 2 wins; Red 2 -> Yellow 1, Red 4, Yellow 2 wins). Hint: Two players, load 241431516, click Hint -> column 3. Threats: Two players, load 11523213371, toggle Show threats -> exactly one ring, yellow, at column 4 row 2 (column 4 is still empty); none for Red. Keyboard: press 5 -> a disc in column 5; ArrowLeft/Right move the marker and Enter drops. Full column: 111111 then click column 1 -> shake. Undo vs the computer: drop, wait 1000, Undo -> both discs gone. Timing: Hard replies in under ~2 s (screenshot during 'Thinking…'). Records: finish a game vs the computer, reload action, the per-level record persists.

rubric.criterion: A 7x6 blue board with round holes and red and yellow discs, plus a panel with the turn and move number, the position code with Load, mode/color/level choices, Hint, Show threats, Undo, New game and a session scoreboard.
Discs drop to the lowest free cell with a bounce by click, digit keys and the Left/Right marker with Enter, and a full column shakes and refuses the drop.

Results are exact with the four discs ringed and the rest dimmed: 1212121 and the diagonal 12233434544 give 'Red wins!', 1223344345 gives 'Yellow wins!', the 42-move hint code gives 'Draw', and the board then accepts no drops.
The position code tracks every move, and Load rejects 48, 1111111 and 12121212 with 'Invalid code' while keeping the current game.
vs Computer as Red, loading 11223 makes the computer block in column 4 at every level, and as Yellow every level opens in column 4.
The levels follow the stated search exactly: after loading 241431516 as Red, the computer plays column 4 on Easy, column 5 on Medium and column 3 on Hard.
After Hard's column 3 in that position the computer wins within its next two moves whatever Red plays, and Hint on 241431516 marks column 3.
Show threats on 11523213371 marks exactly one cell, a yellow ring at column 4 row 2, even though column 4 is still empty.
The computer shows 'Thinking…' and replies within about 2 s even on Hard, and Undo vs the computer removes both your move and its reply.
The session scoreboard counts wins and draws, and the per-level record against the computer survives a reload.

A polished look a designer would accept: glossy discs with a highlight, a blue board with depth, a smooth drop-and-bounce, clear win highlighting, and board and panel side by side in 1280x800 without overlap.

title: Flipside: Othello with flip previews, passes, transcripts and a two-level computer with a weight table
prompt:
Build an Othello (Reversi) game called Flipside: a deep green felt 8 x 8 board with thin dark lines and four small star points, column letters a-h across the top and row numbers 1-8 down the left side (a1 is the top-left square, as in Othello transcripts), glossy black and white discs that flip with a quick 3D turn, and a side panel in Inter or Roboto.

Rules: white starts on d4 and e5, black on d5 and e4, and Black moves first. A move must outflank: the new disc flips every straight line (in all 8 directions) of opponent discs closed off by another disc of the mover, and a square that would flip nothing is illegal. Legal squares show small dots (they can be turned off in Settings), and hovering a legal square previews the discs it would flip with their count. A side with no legal move must pass: show 'Black has no moves – pass' (or White) and the other side moves again. When neither side can move, the game ends with the result and the final count, black first: 'Black wins 40–24', 'White wins 13–51' or 'Draw 32–32'. Show live disc counts, whose turn it is and the move list.

Transcript: the panel shows the game as squares in order (e.g. f5d6c3), passes omitted. 'Load' replays a pasted transcript from the start; if a move in it is illegal, show 'Invalid transcript at move N' and keep the current game. Undo and Redo step through the moves (vs the computer, Undo takes back your move and its reply).

Computer: 'Two players' or 'vs Computer' (you play Black or White) at two levels.
- Level 1 plays the move that flips the most discs; ties go to the first square in reading order (a1, b1 … h1, a2 … h8).
- Level 2 searches 4 plies with alpha-beta (its own move is ply 1, and a forced pass counts as a ply) and keeps the first best move in reading order. A position at the depth limit is scored for the computer as the sum of the square weights below for its discs minus the weights for the opponent's discs, plus 5 x (its number of legal moves - the opponent's); a finished game scores 1000 x (its discs - the opponent's discs).
100 -20 10 5 5 10 -20 100
-20 -50 -2 -2 -2 -2 -50 -20
10 -2 -1 -1 -1 -1 -2 10
5 -2 -1 -1 -1 -1 -2 5
5 -2 -1 -1 -1 -1 -2 5
10 -2 -1 -1 -1 -1 -2 10
-20 -50 -2 -2 -2 -2 -50 -20
100 -20 10 5 5 10 -20 100
The computer replies about 500 ms after your move, and at once when a loaded transcript leaves it to move. 'Hint' marks the Level 2 choice for the side to move. Keep a record of wins, draws and losses against each level in localStorage.
interaction_hints: Each interact call opens a fresh page. Squares: a-h are columns left to right, 1-8 rows top to bottom (get the board rectangle with eval getBoundingClientRect). All facts were computed with the stated rules and search. Start: Black's dots are exactly d3, c4, f5, e6; hovering d3 previews 1 flip. Two players, click f5 -> e5 turns black (4-1) and White's dots are f4, d6, f6. Pass: Two players, load f5f6c4g5h5h4f7h6 -> 'Black has no moves – pass' and White is to move again, with only c5 and e7 legal (count 8-4). Wipeout: load d3c3b3d2e1d6d7e3f4 -> the game ends at once with 'Black wins 13–0'. Draw: load f5f6c4g5h5f4g7c5g6f7c6h4e6d6f8b5a5b4b3e7f3f2d7h6f1a2b2b6c7e8g4e2d3d2c2d1d8e3c3c8e1a4b8g8a6a1a3a7c1b1h3b7h8h7g3g1g2h1h2a8 (60 moves, one pass) -> 'Draw 32–32'. Invalid: load f5f5 -> 'Invalid transcript at move 2', board unchanged. Level 1: vs Computer as Black, Level 1, click f5 -> the computer plays f4 (every reply flips 1; f4 is first in reading order); vs Computer as White, Level 1, load f5f6e6f4 -> the computer (Black) plays c3 at once. Level 2: as Black, click f5 -> the computer plays d6 (root values f4 -14, d6 -7, f6 -19); as White, load f5f6e6f4 -> it plays e3 at once. Hint: Two players, load f5d6c3d3c4 (White to move), click Hint -> b3; load f5f6e6f4 and Hint -> e3. Undo/Redo: a few moves, Undo twice, Redo once, compare the board with the transcript. Record: vs Computer as Black (either level), load d3c3b3d2e1d6d7e3 (Black to move), click f4 -> 'Black wins 13–0'; reload action, the record shows the win.

rubric.criterion: The board shows a-h across the top and 1-8 down the side with a1 top-left and the standard start (white d4 and e5, black d5 and e4), plus live disc counts, the turn, the transcript with Load, Undo/Redo, mode, color and level choices and Hint.
Legal moves are exact: Black starts with dots on d3, c4, f5 and e6 only, after f5 White's dots are f4, d6 and f6, and hovering a legal square previews its flips with the count.
A move flips exactly the outflanked lines with a flip animation, and clicking an illegal square changes nothing.
Loading f5f6c4g5h5h4f7h6 shows 'Black has no moves – pass' and White moves again with only c5 and e7 legal.
Loading d3c3b3d2e1d6d7e3f4 ends the game at once with 'Black wins 13–0', and the 60-move hint transcript ends with 'Draw 32–32'.
The transcript always matches the moves played, and loading f5f5 shows 'Invalid transcript at move 2' while keeping the current game.
Level 1 follows its rule: as Black, after f5 the computer plays f4, and as White, loading f5f6e6f4 makes the computer play c3 at once.
Level 2 follows the search: as Black, after f5 the computer plays d6; as White, loading f5f6e6f4 makes it play e3; and Hint after f5d6c3d3c4 marks b3.
Undo and Redo walk through the moves (a pair vs the computer), and the record of wins, draws and losses per level survives a reload.
Board and side panel fit side by side in 1280x800 with square cells, discs centered in them and coordinates aligned to their rows and columns.
A cohesive felt-table look a designer would accept: glossy discs with soft shadows, a smooth flip animation, subtle legal-move dots and a clear, well-aligned side panel.

title: Kingrow: American checkers with compulsory multi-jumps, crowning, PDN positions and a searching computer
prompt:
Build American checkers (English draughts) called Kingrow: a warm wooden 8 x 8 board, charcoal Black pieces and ivory White pieces drawn as round discs with a rim and a soft shadow, kings marked with a gold crown, and a side panel in Inter or Roboto.

Board and notation: rows 1-8 run top to bottom and play uses the dark squares only: columns 2, 4, 6, 8 on odd rows and 1, 3, 5, 7 on even rows. Number them 1-32 in reading order (1-4 on row 1, 5-8 on row 2 … 29-32 on row 8) and show the numbers small in a corner of each dark square. Black starts on 1-12 and moves first, going down the board; White starts on 21-32 and moves up. The board always shows White at the bottom.

Rules: a man steps diagonally forward to an empty square; a king steps diagonally in any of the four directions. A capture jumps a diagonally adjacent enemy piece onto the empty square right behind it and removes it. Capturing is compulsory: when any capture exists the side to move must capture (any capture; there is no rule to take the most), and a capturing piece keeps jumping while it can, choosing its route at branches. A man that reaches the far row is crowned and its move ends there, even if it could jump on. A side with no pieces or no legal move loses ('Black wins' / 'White wins'). The third time the same position occurs with the same side to move, the game is a 'Draw by repetition'.

Interaction: click a piece to show its legal landing squares (when a capture is compulsory, other pieces only shake), then click the landing square; in a multi-jump click each landing square in turn. Dragging also works. Highlight the last move. The move list uses standard notation numbered per full move: '11-15' for a move, '15x22' for a capture and '27x18x9' for a multi-jump (e.g. '1. 11-15 22-18 2. 15x22'). A 'Position' box always shows the position in PDN FEN form, e.g. 'B:W21,22,K30:B1,2,K14' (side to move, then White's and Black's squares, K marking kings), and loads a pasted one; bad text shows 'Invalid position' and keeps the game, and a loaded position that is already decided shows its result at once.

Computer: 'Two players' or 'vs Computer' (you choose Black or White) with Easy (2 plies) and Hard (6 plies). It uses minimax with alpha-beta, a whole multi-jump being one ply. A position at the depth limit scores 100 per man and 160 per king, the computer's minus the opponent's; a side to move with no legal move has lost, scoring 100000 - ply for the winner (negative when the computer is the loser). Moves are tried in order of their starting square, then their landing squares, and the first best is kept. It replies about 500 ms after your move, and at once when a loaded position leaves it to move. Also: Undo (vs the computer, your move and its reply), New game, captured-piece counts, and a record of results against each level in localStorage.
interaction_hints: Each interact call opens a fresh page. Square s is on row ceil(s/4); dark squares are columns 2,4,6,8 on odd rows and 1,3,5,7 on even rows (get the board rectangle with eval). Paste positions into the Position box. All facts were checked with a rules engine and the stated search. Start: Black's legal moves are exactly 9-13, 9-14, 10-14, 10-15, 11-15, 11-16, 12-16. Forced capture: Two players, 11-15 then 22-18: only the man on 15 can move and its only target is 22 (15x22); the list reads '1. 11-15 22-18 2. 15x22'. Branching double jump: load 'B:W14,22,23:B1,9' -> the only moves are 9x18x25 and 9x18x27 (click 18, then 25 or 27); both white men jumped disappear. Crowning stops a jump: load 'B:W5,26,27:B1,22' -> Black must play 22x31, the man is crowned on 31 and the move ends with the white man on 27 still there (White then has 27-23 or 27-24); then check the new king can move backwards. No moves: load 'B:W8,11:B4' -> 'White wins' at once. Repetition: load 'B:WK29:BK4', play 4-8, 29-25, 8-4, 25-29, 4-8, 29-25, 8-4, 25-29 -> 'Draw by repetition' after the 8th move. Computer: vs Computer, you Black, Hard, load 'W:W13,22,24,25,26,27,28,29,30,32:B1,3,4,5,6,7,11,12,14,16' (White to move) -> the computer plays 24-19 at once (root values: 24-19 +200, others 0 or -100); your only move is 16x23; the computer answers 27x18x9x2, capturing three men and crowning on 2. Same position on Easy -> 24-20. Start as White vs Hard -> the computer opens 9-13 (all moves tie; first in order). Invalid: paste 'hello' -> 'Invalid position'. Undo vs the computer removes a pair. Record: vs Computer, you Black, load 'B:W18:B14' and play 14x23 -> 'Black wins'; reload action, the record shows the win.

rubric.criterion: An 8x8 board playing on dark squares numbered 1-32 as described, Black on 1-12 at the top and White on 21-32 at the bottom, with a move list, a Position box, mode/color/level choices, Undo and New game.
From the start Black has exactly the seven moves 9-13, 9-14, 10-14, 10-15, 11-15, 11-16 and 12-16, shown as targets when pieces are clicked, and men never move backwards.
Captures are compulsory: after 11-15 22-18 only the man on 15 can move and it must play 15x22, and the list reads '1. 11-15 22-18 2. 15x22'.
Multi-jumps: in 'B:W14,22,23:B1,9' the man on 9 must jump twice and may choose 9x18x25 or 9x18x27, written that way, removing both jumped men.
Crowning ends the move: in 'B:W5,26,27:B1,22' Black plays 22x31, the piece is crowned on 31 and stops with the white man on 27 still on the board, and kings then move and capture backwards.
Endings: loading 'B:W8,11:B4' shows 'White wins' at once, taking the last enemy piece wins, and the king shuffle from 'B:WK29:BK4' ends in 'Draw by repetition' after 8 moves.

The Hard computer follows the search: as Black, loading 'W:W13,22,24,25,26,27,28,29,30,32:B1,3,4,5,6,7,11,12,14,16' makes it play 24-19 at once, and after your forced 16x23 it replies 27x18x9x2, crowning on 2.
The Easy computer plays 24-20 in that same position, and the Hard computer opens 9-13 when you play White.

The Position box shows the current PDN FEN, loads valid positions including kings and rejects junk with 'Invalid position'; Undo vs the computer takes back a pair, and the per-level record survives a reload.
The board with its small square numbers, the move list and the controls fit in 1280x800 without overlap, and the move list scrolls when it grows.
A warm wooden board a game artist would accept: discs with a rim and shadow, clear gold crowns on kings, and visible selection, target and last-move highlights.

title: Broadside: Battleship with seeded fleets, a hunt-and-target computer, water marking and stats
prompt:
Build a Battleship game called Broadside against the computer: two 10 x 10 sea grids side by side (your fleet on the left, enemy waters on the right) with rows A-J from the top and columns 1-10, a navy-and-steel naval look, ships drawn as rounded grey hulls, white pegs for misses and red bursts for hits, Inter or Roboto type. Cells are named like C7 (row letter, then column).

Fleet: Carrier 5, Battleship 4, Cruiser 3, Submarine 3, Destroyer 2. Ships lie horizontally or vertically and may not overlap or touch, not even diagonally.

Setup: drag ships from a dock onto your grid (R or a right click rotates the ship being placed; an invalid spot shows a red preview and refuses the drop) or press 'Random'. 'Clear' empties your grid, and 'Start battle' is enabled only when all five ships are placed.

Randomness: a Seed field (default 1; ?seed=N also works) and mulberry32:
function mulberry32(a){return function(){a|=0;a=a+0x6D2B79F5|0;let t=Math.imul(a^a>>>15,1|a);t=t+Math.imul(t^t>>>7,61|t)^t;return((t^t>>>14)>>>0)/4294967296;}}
Random placement places the ships in fleet order; for each ship, list every valid spot (first all horizontal spots in reading order of their left end, then all vertical spots in reading order of their top end) and take index floor(rand() x count). The enemy fleet uses mulberry32(seed). Your 'Random' button uses one mulberry32(seed + 1) stream per game: each press places a whole new fleet from the next values. title: Grid Nine: Sudoku with notes, auto-candidates, technique-named hints, a mistake limit and a validating importer
prompt:
Build a Sudoku game called Grid Nine with a crisp editorial look: white cells, thin grey cell lines and thick 3x3 box lines, givens in bold near-black, your entries in blue, small grey notes, and Inter or Roboto with tabular digits. Build the grid from DOM cells carrying data-row and data-col attributes (1-based) so our test scripts can target them.

Puzzles (81 characters in reading order; 0 or '.' is empty):
Easy 530070000600195000098000060800060003400803001700020006060000280000419005000080079
Medium 4..2...8.....7..9319....5.2..61.5.........9...5..43.......26..424.....3.7..4.....
Hard 800000000003600000070090200050007000000045700000100030001000068008500010090000400

Entry: select a cell by clicking or with the arrow keys; 1-9 places a digit (keys or an on-screen pad) and Backspace, Delete or 0 clears it; givens are locked. Notes mode (N key or a pencil toggle) toggles small candidate digits laid out 3 x 3 in the cell instead. 'Auto notes' fills every empty cell with its candidates (the digits not yet in its row, column or box). Placing a digit removes it from the notes of every cell in the same row, column and box. Highlight the selected cell's row, column and box and every cell holding the same digit. A digit that repeats in a row, column or box turns red, together with the cell it clashes with. The pad shows how many of each digit are still missing and greys out a digit once all nine are placed.

Hint (H or a button) names the technique and fills the cell. It first looks for a naked single: the first empty cell in reading order with exactly one candidate ('Naked single: r5c5 = 5'). Otherwise it looks for a hidden single, checking rows 1-9, then columns 1-9, then boxes 1-9 (boxes in reading order), and in the first unit that has one, the smallest digit that fits in only one of its cells ('Hidden single: 6 in column 1 → r2c1'). Candidates always come from the placed digits, not from your notes. If neither exists, show 'No single found – try notes'.

Mistakes: a digit that differs from the solution counts as a mistake ('Mistakes 1/3'); the third one ends the game with 'Game over' unless 'Mistake limit' is switched off in Settings. Undo and Redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y) cover digits and notes. A timer runs, with a pause button that hides the grid. Completing the grid shows 'Solved in m:ss'. Best times per difficulty and the game in progress survive a reload (localStorage).

Import: paste 81 characters and press 'Import'. Show 'Needs 81 cells' for a wrong length; 'Duplicate 5 in row 1' (or column 3, box 7 …; check rows, then columns, then boxes, and report the first clash) for clashing givens; otherwise solve it and show 'No solution' or 'Multiple solutions', or start it as a Custom puzzle when the solution is unique.
interaction_hints: Each interact call opens a fresh page. Target cells with selectors like [data-row='5'][data-col='5']. All facts were computed with a solver. Easy's solution: 534678912672195348198342567859761423426853791713924856961537284287419635345286179. Hints on Easy: 'Naked single: r5c5 = 5', then r5c2 = 2, then r5c8 = 9. Medium has no naked single at the start and no hidden single in any row: hints are 'Hidden single: 6 in column 1 → r2c1', then 5 in column 1 at r7c1, then 6 in column 2 at r9c2. Hard (Inkala's puzzle) -> 'No single found – try notes'. Auto notes on Easy: r1c3 shows 1 2 4, r1c4 shows 2 6, r9c1 shows 1 2 3; then place 4 at r1c3 (correct): 4 disappears from the notes of r1c6, r1c7, r1c8, r1c9, r2c2, r2c3, r7c3 and r9c3. Mistake: Easy, type 1 at r1c3 (wrong, but no clash) -> 'Mistakes 1/3'; type 5 at r1c3 -> it turns red together with r1c1; three wrong digits -> 'Game over'. Import (paste into the import box): '123' -> 'Needs 81 cells'; Easy with r1c3 = 5 (535070000600195000098000060800060003400803001700020006060000280000419005000080079) -> 'Duplicate 5 in row 1'; Easy with r1c3 = 1 (531070000600195000098000060800060003400803001700020006060000280000419005000080079) -> 'No solution'; Easy without its r3c3 given (530070000600195000090000060800060003400803001700020006060000280000419005000080079) -> 'Multiple solutions'. Solve: type the Easy solution into the empty cells (reading order) -> 'Solved in m:ss'; reload action -> best time shown. Progress: place a few digits, reload -> restored. Undo/Redo: Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y over a digit and a note. Pause hides the grid and stops the timer (two screenshots 1.5 s apart).

rubric.criterion: Easy, Medium and Hard load exactly the given puzzles with bold locked givens, and the page has a 1-9 pad with remaining counts, a Notes toggle, Auto notes, Hint, Undo/Redo, a timer, a mistakes counter and Import.
Cells are selected by click and arrow keys and filled by keys and the pad, the row, column, box and same digits are highlighted, and givens cannot be changed.
Auto notes on Easy gives exactly 1 2 4 at r1c3, 2 6 at r1c4 and 1 2 3 at r9c1, and placing a digit removes it from its peers' notes.
Hints on Easy follow the stated order: 'Naked single: r5c5 = 5', then r5c2 = 2, then r5c8 = 9.
Medium's first hints are hidden singles found by columns: 6 at r2c1 and 5 at r7c1 in column 1, then 6 at r9c2 in column 2, and Hard shows 'No single found – try notes'.
A repeated digit turns red with the cell it clashes with, and wrong digits count 'Mistakes 1/3' with the third ending the game unless the limit is off.
Import rejects '123' with 'Needs 81 cells', Easy with a 5 at r1c3 with 'Duplicate 5 in row 1', Easy with a 1 at r1c3 with 'No solution' and Easy without its r3c3 given with 'Multiple solutions'.
Entering the Easy solution shows 'Solved in m:ss', and the best time and an unfinished game in progress survive a reload.
Undo and Redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y) cover digits and notes, and pause hides the grid and stops the timer.
The 9x9 grid is square with thicker 3x3 box lines, notes sit in a 3x3 pattern inside cells, and grid, pad and panel fit in 1280x800 without overlap.
A crisp, readable look a designer would accept: givens, entries and notes clearly distinct, subtle highlight colors and a consistent type scale.

title: River Hop: Frogger with exact lane patterns, diving turtles, home bays, flies, a timer and faster levels
prompt:
Build a Frogger-style arcade game called River Hop on a canvas with a bright retro look: a purple median and start strip, a dark road with dashed lane lines, a deep blue river with brown logs and red-shelled turtles, a green hedge with five home bays at the top, a green frog seen from above that faces the way it hops, and chunky pixel-style text. Keep drawing light (simple shapes, no per-pixel effects) so it runs smoothly without a GPU.

Field: 13 columns x 13 rows of 48 px cells (row 1 on top). Row 1 is the hedge with home bays at columns 1, 4, 7, 10 and 13; rows 2-6 are river, row 7 the median, rows 8-12 road and row 13 the start. The frog starts at row 13, column 7.

Lanes: each lane repeats its pattern forever ('.' is a gap; each other letter is one cell of an object: L log, T turtle, D diving turtle, K truck, C car, B bulldozer) and scrolls smoothly at the given speed in cells per second; when a level starts, column 1 shows the pattern's first character.
Row 2 logs, moving right at 1.5: LLLL...LLLL....
Row 3 turtles, moving left at 2: TT...DD...TT...
Row 4 logs, moving right at 2.5: LLLLLL......
Row 5 logs, moving right at 1: LLL...LLL....
Row 6 turtles, moving left at 1.5: DDD..TTT..TTT....
Row 8 trucks, moving left at 1.2: KK......KK.....
Row 9 cars, moving right at 2.4: C.....C.......
Row 10 cars, moving left at 1.6: C...C........
Row 11 bulldozers, moving right at 1: B...B...B.......
Row 12 cars, moving left at 2: C....C.....
Diving turtles repeat a 5 s cycle: 3 s surfaced, 0.5 s sinking (half under, still safe), 1 s under water (the frog drowns), 0.5 s rising (safe).

Frog: arrow keys or WASD hop exactly one cell (a 120 ms hop; keys during a hop are ignored), and it cannot leave the field sideways or downwards. On a log or turtle it drifts with it, so it can end up between columns; being carried off the side kills it. Landing in water or on a fully sunk turtle, touching a vehicle, or landing on the hedge or in a filled bay kills it. A bay is entered when the frog lands on row 1 with its center within half a cell of the bay's center.

Timer and score: each frog has 30 s, shown as a shrinking bar; running out kills it. Score 10 for each hop onto a row this frog has not reached before, and 50 per frog home plus 10 per whole second left. Every 7 s a fly appears for 4 s in an empty bay chosen as index floor(rand() x empty bays), with rand from mulberry32(level); a frog reaching the fly's bay gets 200 more. Filling all five bays scores 1000 and starts the next level with empty bays and every lane 25 percent faster than before.
function mulberry32(a){return function(){a|=0;a=a+0x6D2B79F5|0;let t=Math.imul(a^a>>>15,1|a);t=t+Math.imul(t^t>>>7,61|t)^t;return((t^t>>>14)>>>0)/4294967296;}}

Lives: 3, shown as frog icons; a death plays a short splat or splash and the next frog starts at row 13. Losing the last one shows 'GAME OVER' and a TOP 5 (3-letter initials, score, level) saved in localStorage. A title screen starts with Enter; P pauses. HUD: score, hi-score, lives, level and the timer bar.

QA debug mode with ?debug=1 in the URL: F freezes or unfreezes every lane and the turtle cycle, I toggles invincibility (no deaths, but logs still carry the frog), N fills the bays at columns 1, 4, 10 and 13, and T sets the current frog's timer to 3 s.
interaction_hints: Each interact call opens a fresh page; use --entry 'index.html?debug=1' and press Enter to start. Lanes: press f right after Enter and screenshot: compare each lane with its pattern (it may have shifted a cell or two since the start) and unfreeze with f; screenshots 1 s apart show row 4 moving fastest in the river and row 5 slowest, logs to the right, turtles to the left, rows 8, 10, 12 to the left and rows 9, 11 to the right. Scoring rule: Enter, press f and i, then ArrowUp (row 12, score 10), ArrowDown, ArrowUp (back on row 12: still 10), ArrowUp (row 11: 20). Walls: ArrowLeft 8 times from the start -> the frog stops at column 1. Road death: plain page (no debug keys pressed), Enter, ArrowUp, wait up to 6 s with screenshots every 500 ms: a row 12 car runs the frog over, splat, lives 3 -> 2, a new frog at row 13 col 7. Riding: debug, Enter, press i (invincible), hop up onto a row 6 turtle group (the frog drifts left with it) and then onto a row 5 log (it drifts right); press i again and stay: carried off the right edge, the frog dies. Drowning: without i, hop from the median into row 6 when no turtle is above -> splash. Diving: stand on a D group in row 6 (with i off) for 5 s -> it sinks and the frog drowns. Home bay: debug, Enter, press f, i, n (bays 1, 4, 10, 13 filled), then ArrowUp 12 times (delay_ms 200): the frog reaches bay 7 -> +50, +10 per whole second left, +1000, 'LEVEL 2' with empty bays; unfreeze and compare lane speed with level 1 (about 25 percent faster). Fly: watch the bays for ~10 s: a fly shows in an empty bay for ~4 s (with f, i, n pressed, reaching it adds 200). Timer: debug, Enter, press t -> the bar nearly empties and after 3 s the frog dies. Game over: plain page, stand on row 12 until three frogs are lost (or hop into the river) -> 'GAME OVER', type initials, Enter, reload action, TOP 5 on the title. Pause: p, two screenshots 500 ms apart unchanged.

rubric.criterion: The 13x13 field has the hedge with five bays at columns 1, 4, 7, 10 and 13, five river lanes, a median, five road lanes and a start strip, with the frog starting at row 13 column 7.

Each lane matches its pattern, object type and direction: logs moving right in rows 2, 4 and 5, turtles moving left in rows 3 and 6, vehicles moving left in rows 8, 10 and 12 and right in rows 9 and 11, with row 4 visibly the fastest river lane and row 5 the slowest.
Each key press hops exactly one cell and the frog cannot leave the field; 10 points come only for rows this frog has not reached before (Up, Down, Up from the start leaves 10, one more Up makes 20).
Deaths work: a vehicle kills the frog, open water drowns it, and being carried off the side on a log kills it; each costs a life with a splat or splash and the next frog starts at row 13.
The frog rides logs and turtles, drifting with them between columns.
Diving turtles run the 5 s cycle (surfaced, half under, fully under, rising) and a frog on them when fully under drowns.
Reaching bay 7 after debug N adds 50, 10 per whole second left and 1000 for the fifth bay, then 'LEVEL 2' starts with empty bays and lanes about 25 percent faster.
A fly appears in an empty bay for about 4 s and reaching it adds 200.
The 30 s timer bar shrinks and running out (debug T) kills the frog; losing the last life shows 'GAME OVER', initials enter a TOP 5 that survives a reload, and P pauses.
The 624x624 field is centered and fully visible in 1280x800 with the score, lives, level and timer bar around it without overlap.
A bright, cohesive retro look a game artist would accept: readable logs, turtles and vehicles, a frog that faces its hop direction with a hop animation, and clear splat and splash effects.

title: Star Forge: idle clicker with exact cost curves, upgrades, number formatting, prestige cores and offline earnings
prompt:
Build an idle clicker game called Star Forge with a deep-space look: a big glowing asteroid in the middle that pulses when clicked and shows a floating '+1', a generator shop on the right with simple drawn icons, an upgrades strip, and a stats panel; Inter or Roboto with tabular numbers.

Economy (ore):
- Clicking the asteroid gives 1 ore (times the core bonus below).
- Generators (base cost / ore per second each): Drone 15 / 0.1, Miner 100 / 1, Smelter 1,100 / 8, Freighter 12,000 / 47, Station 130,000 / 260, Ring World 1,400,000 / 1,400. The next unit costs ceil(base x 1.15^owned). A buy mode switch offers x1, x10 and Max: x10 costs the sum of the next ten unit prices, and Max buys units one by one while affordable. Buy buttons show the cost and are disabled, with the cost in red, when you cannot pay. A generator row stays hidden as '???' until your ore has at some point reached half its base cost (Drones are always shown).
- Upgrades: each generator has three upgrades that each double its output, unlocked at 10, 25 and 50 owned and costing 50, 500 and 5,000 times its base cost. 'Resonant Pick' (unlocked once 1,000 ore has been mined in total, cost 5,000) makes each click also add 5 percent of your ore per second.
- Production is continuous (update at least 10 times per second). The header shows ore and ore per second.

Numbers: below 1,000 show at most one decimal ('16', '3.4'); from 1,000 up show three significant digits, rounded down, with a K, M, B or T suffix ('1.01K', '3.28K', '45.6M'). Costs use the same format.

Prestige: 'Collapse' becomes available once this run has mined 1,000,000 ore in total. It resets ore, generators and upgrades and grants floor(sqrt(ore mined this run / 1,000,000)) cores; each core adds 10 percent to all production and clicks. Show the cores you have and how many a collapse would give now.

Saving: autosave to localStorage every 5 s and after every purchase. On load, add offline earnings of 50 percent of the saved ore per second for the time away (at most 8 hours) and show 'While you were away (1h 0m): +11.5K ore'. 'Export save' shows a text code, 'Import save' loads one ('Invalid save' for bad input), and 'Reset' asks for confirmation first.

Stats panel: ore mined this run and all time, total clicks and time played.

QA debug mode with ?debug=1 in the URL: the game clock is frozen so numbers stay exact (passive production only happens through the buttons below and offline earnings), and a debug bar offers '+1K ore' and '+1M ore' (both count as mined), '+60 s' (adds 60 seconds of production at once) and 'Away 1h' (moves the save's timestamp one hour back and reloads).
interaction_hints: Each interact call opens a fresh page (start from a clean state: if a save exists, use Reset first or eval localStorage.clear() then reload). Use --entry 'index.html?debug=1' for exact numbers. All facts were computed with the stated formulas. Clicks: 15 clicks -> ore 15; buy a Drone -> ore 0, next Drone 18; Drone prices run 15, 18, 20, 23, 27, 31, 35, 40, 46, 53 (x10 from zero costs 308). Scenario (debug, fresh): '+1K ore' -> 1,000 shown as '1.00K' (Smelter row revealed since 550 was reached, Freighter still '???'); mode Max, buy Drones -> 17 Drones, ore '16', '1.7' per second, next Drone '162', x10 price '3.28K'; the first Drone upgrade (unlocked at 10 owned) costs 750. '+1K ore' -> '1.01K'; buy the Drone upgrade -> ore 266, '3.4' per second; '+60 s' -> ore 470; Max on Miners -> 3 Miners (100 + 115 + 133), ore 122, '6.4' per second; 'Away 1h' -> after the reload 'While you were away (1h 0m): +11.5K ore' (0.5 x 6.4 x 3600 = 11,520) and ore '11.6K' (11,642). Resonant Pick shows once 1,000 has been mined (cost 5,000). Prestige (debug, fresh): '+1M ore' four times -> Collapse available, offering 2 cores (floor(sqrt(4))); collapse -> ore 0, no generators or upgrades, 2 cores; a click then adds 1.2 ore ('+1.2'). Disabled: with 16 ore and buy mode x1, the Miner button (100) is disabled with a red cost. Save: Export save, copy the code, Reset (confirm), Import the code -> the same generators and ore; import 'hello' -> 'Invalid save'. Plain page (no debug): ore per second actually accumulates over time and a reload keeps progress.

rubric.criterion: The page shows the clickable asteroid, ore and ore per second, the six generators with later ones as '???' until revealed, the x1/x10/Max switch, upgrades, Collapse with core info, a stats panel and Export/Import/Reset.
Clicking adds 1 ore with a floating '+1', and Drone prices run 15, 18, 20, 23, 27 as Drones are bought, with x10 from zero costing 308.
With debug '+1K ore' and Max, Drones buys exactly 17, leaving '16' ore at '1.7' per second, with the next Drone at '162' and x10 at '3.28K'.

'Away 1h' shows 'While you were away (1h 0m): +11.5K ore' and the ore then reads '11.6K' (half of an hour's production added).
Number formatting follows the rules: at most one decimal below 1,000 and three significant digits rounded down with K/M suffixes above ('1.01K' for 1,016).
Four '+1M ore' presses enable Collapse offering 2 cores; collapsing resets ore, generators and upgrades, keeps 2 cores, and a click then gives 1.2 ore.
Unaffordable buttons are disabled with red costs, generator rows unlock at half their base cost (Smelter after 550 ore, Freighter still hidden at 1,000), and Resonant Pick unlocks at 1,000 ore mined.
Progress survives a reload, Export then Import restores the same state, an invalid code shows 'Invalid save', and Reset asks for confirmation.
A polished space look a designer would accept: a glowing asteroid with click feedback, a tidy shop with icons, tabular numbers that do not jitter, and consistent spacing within 1280x800.
